newsitem.title: USA: Wang suit reopened by appeals court.
newsitem.headline: Wang suit reopened by appeals court.

text.p: An antitrust lawsuit against Wang Laboratories Corp will return to U.S. District Court in Denver after a federal appeals court reversed itself and reopened the case, an attorney for Wang said on Wednesday.
The suit, filed by a Wang competitor, Systemcare Inc, alleges the company violated antitrust law by requiring purchasers of its software support services to buy its hardware support services.
Twelve judges of the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver on Tuesday reversed a three-judge panel of the court, which last year upheld a summary judgment in favor of Wang.

The Wang attorney, Jerrold Ganzfried, told Reuters on Wednesday the latest ruling would send the case back to the district court for consideration of a motion for summary judgment on additional grounds.
Systemcare services Wang-built computer hardware in Colorado.
Tuesday's ruling said a contract between a buyer and seller in which the seller coerces a buyer's acquiescence in a tying arrangement is sufficient under antitrust law for a lawsuit to proceed.
Wang denied it conditioned the purchase of software support on the purchase of hardware maintenance, except when a service contract was in effect.
